reconciliation_brief:
# Final instruction reconciliation

Perform the same bounded, independent, read-only consultation as review-brief-v1.md (read that original brief in full). This is a fresh review round, not permission to execute donor procedures, edit, commit, fetch, delegate, or run executor trials. Read the complete five frozen candidate-v2 packages against baseline, with the original governing instructions and pinned donor context. Return specific remaining defects and affected-point dispositions with evidence and limits. Prior findings are supplied for reconciliation; do not treat a prior verdict as authority.

Read astra-review-v1.json and fable-review-v1.md in this directory in full. The coordinator's current dispositions follow.

## Resolved scope

The user's upstream request explicitly covered every origin.txt using Matt or pstack, followed by approval to do all proposed work. Advancing the 26 resolved source cursors is authorized metadata maintenance in this Update run, including the 15 ranges outside the five behavior targets. Preserve immutable baseline_commit/baseline_paths and all other-author source records. No non-target skill instruction changes. The error-handling plugin version change is an explicit metadata-only skip. Six cursors already at the candidate remain unchanged. No push, installation, or PR.

## Changes addressing Astra

- A1: debug's entrypoint now loads investigation for performance-related issues, including fast deterministic resource regressions. Memory-only fixture was frozen before either corresponding arm started.
- A2: an adoption decision must resolve material configuration differences or justify them from the user's actual constraints. Identifying a handicap is insufficient; absent evidence/authority leaves the choice unresolved. Narrow as-deployed observations remain valid.
- A3: verify says performance-regression rather than regression.
- A4: failure rejection and valid acceptance are separate outcomes. Reconstructed cases are labeled from the confirmed contract; absent meaningful cases leaves proof unresolved.
- A5: debug/prototype maintenance wording and direct optional verify dependencies distinguish runtime assessment from maintenance authoring.

## Changes addressing Fable

- F1: debug and prototype retain a compact correctness/comparability/counts/units/variation fallback, explicitly including warm-up/cache conditions. Prototype passes the harness and rerun command. The shared specialist still owns the detailed evidence criteria. Added matched missing-verify trials are planned.
- F2: workflow-to-skill names the enforcement owner and routes rather than executes a structural remedy. It distinguishes project-level enforcement by the authorized existing project owner from skill-bundled helper implementation by the instruction writer. Both need failure/control executions before claiming enforcement. Extraction-only authority remains explicit.
- F3: performance-regression wording was already corrected for Astra.
- F4: performance evidence explicitly allows supplied packets/harnesses without a local application recipe and reports missing application coverage separately.
- F5: verify explicitly returns to the active debug/prototype caller without starting another investigation or experiment. Debug owns measurements, cause and repair within authority; verify owns criteria and verdict.
- F6: the donor's fixed minimum runs, compulsory bottleneck proof for every observation, Linux commands, single PR number, hillclimb loop and automatic tuning/PR steps are intentionally not adopted. Provenance will record those deviations and linked playbooks as context read, not direct instruction sources. The existing completion/correctness/budget clauses already require adequate evidence for the specific claim; no redundant report checklist added.
- F7: define comparison/stopping decisions before running; for supplied results check whether they were defined.
- F8: architecture screen preserves exposed private representations as well as reachable internals.
- F9: design names the enforceable mechanism; implementation only within authorized implementation.
- F10: workflow's destination bullet names the existing enforcement owner; the following paragraph adds structural remedy, coverage-before-removal and migration scope.

## Metadata and validation

Provenance cursor movement and final atlas/README changes remain held until checks finish. Architect borrowed/local-choice records will reflect this screen. New pstack-correct record will state no fixed recurrence threshold, forced rule table or exception-expiry default. New verify source records measurement criteria and the deviations above. Debug/prototype dependency metadata already reflects verify; existing prototype local choice will be reconciled with fallback assessment. Complete MIT notices remain valid at unchanged license blobs.

Behavioral outputs are independent supplied-context trials, not proof of installed automatic activation. Baseline architecture and four baseline behavior cases completed; candidate architecture-v1 is still finishing. Candidate-v2 behavior and absent-specialist trials will use matched fixtures/tools/authority/profile with grader expectations excluded. An unchanged passing baseline will not be reported as a demonstrated improvement. The final architecture wording correction will receive an affected execution check on the final candidate.

Review the actual candidate, not this description alone. Identify any material unresolved objection; distinguish a necessary correction from a stylistic preference. No behavioral success is claimed by this consultation.

fable.result:
Review complete. Everything below is from reading the frozen packages, donors, governing references, metadata, and the prepared trial fixtures. I ran no executor and edited nothing.

**Integrity checks passed.** The working tree equals candidate-v1 for all five packages. All twelve donor copies match their blobs at the pinned cursor/plugins head, both recorded baselines are ancestors of it, and the pstack LICENSE blob is identical at every pinned commit, so existing notices remain valid. The architect delta is one commit touching two files, and the trial skill folders are byte-identical to baseline. Two material defects and one scope decision need the coordinator's attention before checks run.

## Findings and corrections

- **Material. The debug and prototype fallback branches lost their measurement contract.** `candidate-v1/debug/references/investigation.md:77-89` removed the baseline rule to keep correctness checks beside measurements and to report sample counts, cache conditions and variability. The prototype reference at `experiment.md:13-20` removed comparable inputs, repetitions, warm-up, units and range. Those rules now exist only in verify, which both skills treat as optional. When verify is absent from the catalog, the debug case `performance-regression` and the prototype case `lookup-experiment` would regress against their own eval expectations. The writing reference forbids deleting a rule as enforced elsewhere without checking that path, and hosts.md says loading a file and invoking a skill differ by host. Correction: keep one fallback sentence in each. Debug: "With or without that assessment, compare correct behavior under comparable conditions and report workload, sample counts, units and variation." Prototype: "Keep inputs, workload, environment and measurement boundary comparable; report repetitions, units and a range rather than one favorable sample, and label unassessed conclusions." Also add the harness and rerun command to the prototype handoff list at line 16, since verify is told to inspect what the harness times.

- **Material. Workflow-to-skill assigns project enforcement to the wrong executor.** `candidate-v1/workflow-to-skill/SKILL.md:104-105` says the writer owns implementation and must run the check on both cases. The writer is `agent-instructions` per lines 8 to 10, which owns skill-bundled helpers, not a project's types, lint or CI. The extraction trial fixture makes this concrete: its OWNERS file gives the layer check to the quality lane and CI. Line 59 also says "prefer removing an invalid path" inside the retention section, while the extraction-only boundary appears only at lines 105 to 106. Correction at line 59: "Route the lesson toward removing the invalid path or enforcing its invariant with existing types, constraints, lint or behavioral checks when the project supports it, and name the existing owner of that enforcement." Correction at lines 104 to 106: "Name the executor. The project's existing check owner implements project-level enforcement under its own authorization; the writer implements a skill-bundled helper. Either must run the check on the failing case and the valid nearby case before claiming enforcement. An extraction-only result proposes that proof and makes no unrequested repository change."

- **Medium.** `candidate-v1/verify/SKILL.md:30` says "or regression claims", which also matches functional regressions named at line 22 and would load the benchmark reference for ordinary bug verification. Change to "or performance-regression claims".

- **Medium.** Verify can be called by prototype or with a supplied packet where no `verify-<app>` recipe exists, and the entrypoint at lines 35 to 50 treats a required missing dependency as a blocker. Add to `performance-evidence.md:3-6`: "A supplied harness, benchmark or results packet can be assessed without a project recipe; the recipe applies when the claim covers application behavior."

- **Medium. Re-entry is implied but not stated.** `performance-evidence.md:67-70` returns the verdict to the caller, yet `verify/SKILL.md:92` routes requested diagnosis to debug, and `investigation.md:80` says verify "owns measurement evidence", which reads as verify performing the measurement. Add to the return section: "When `debug` or `prototype` supplied the claim, return the verdict to it; do not start a new diagnosis or experiment." Change the debug line to "It owns the measurement-evidence criteria and verdict; this skill still measures within its authority."

- **Medium. Donor deviations to record, not reverse.** The reference drops the mandatory limiter from benchmark-checklist question 1 and its report rule, the five-run minimum, the uptime and nproc commands, the single-PR-number rule, and the hillclimb loop. These fit the local no-numeric-defaults pattern, but they must appear in the new source's local choices. Consider one consolidating sentence in the report section: a comparative claim without completed-work and correctness evidence, matched or named conditions, and a budget plausibility check stays inconclusive.

- **Minor.** `performance-evidence.md:12-14` says to define the difference, budget and stopping rule "before tuning", yet line 31 says verification never tunes, and supplied results cannot be defined beforehand. Reword to "before running; for supplied results, check whether they were defined".

- **Minor.** `candidate-v1/design-code-structure/SKILL.md:104` replaced "private representations exposed to callers" with "reachable internals that should be private". Information leakage is now covered only in the conditional state reference. Use "exposed representations or reachable internals that should stay private".

- **Minor.** `design-code-structure/SKILL.md:106-108` says to use project mechanisms to enforce boundaries, which reads as implementation in a design-only request. The architecture trial's tooling note allows import checks only during authorized implementation. Reword to "Name the project's available module, type, lint, test or build mechanism that will enforce each intended boundary; implement it within authorized implementation."

- **Minor.** The bullet at `workflow-to-skill/SKILL.md:55-56` and the new paragraph at lines 59 to 63 both route checks to existing enforcement. Keep the paragraph for ordering, coverage verification and the prevent-new versus migration split only.

The adaptations otherwise read faithfully. The partial-context criterion, derived registries with legitimate projections, one maintained route with retirement planned inside the authorized migration, and the valid-nearby-case proof all preserve the donor's benefit while honoring local scope and authority.

## Provenance and scope

The plan counts are correct: 32 scopes, 26 non-zero ranges, 6 already equal, 2 with deltas. Fifteen of the 26 ranges belong to non-target skills, and the brief both advances all 26 and preserves non-target sources. That is a decision the coordinator must make explicit. Recording an empty range is permitted in Update mode, but it edits origin files outside the frozen five. The error-handling delta is a plugin version bump from 0.15.7 to 0.15.9, a legitimate skip that still needs a review record in that skill's origin file. If the user's approval covered only the three proposals, leave non-target cursors unchanged and report them as Check findings.

For the targets: add a borrowed line and local-choice lines to the architect source for the agent-contributor screen and its deviations. Record pstack-correct with the twice-threshold, AGENTS rule table, and exception-expiry policy skipped. For the new verify source, state that the perf-issue, hillclimb and opening-a-pr playbooks were read as context and their loop and PR rules were not adopted, or include their paths if the coordinator wants to track them. Add an optional `verify` dependency to prototype and debug and revise prototype local choice 51 to reflect assessment plus fallback. README sections for verify, workflow-to-skill and design-code-structure will need the same post-check update as the atlas.

## Behavioral checks and limits

The five prepared fixtures match the changes well. Recommended graded expectations, each as a matched baseline-versus-candidate pair:

- **Performance packet:** dispatch contradicted on unawaited work, errors contradicted on fast rejections, capacity inconclusive from the saturated driver, deployed supported as a configuration difference only, adoption unresolved, micro supported locally but not end to end, rough labeled one observation, valid supported within its limit, functional untouched by any benchmark. Confirm no recipe blocking.
- **Debug route:** verify consulted by name, tracemalloc samples reported with counts and limits, diagnosis continues after assessment, no re-entry into debug from verify, no edits.
- **Prototype route:** the Task returned by alternative B is awaited inside the boundary, outputs compared, uncertainty reported, harness passed to verify.
- **Extraction:** handoff names the quality lane for the check and agent-instructions only for wording, cites the rejected API file plus the test file and good API file as valid nearby cases with the expected message, proposes added-violations-first, excludes the two-bullet preference.
- **Architecture:** UI and billing lists derived as projections, lint import check named but not written, v1 and the relay adapter preserved with planned retirement, the mobile bypass flagged, no alternative manufactured for the label change.
- **Add two arms:** debug and prototype with verify absent from the catalog, to exercise the fallback regression above.

Limits: no runtime was observed and selection probes were not run. The debug-route fixture changed during this consultation, so hash its final state before running. Candidate-arm outputs do not exist yet. I could not see the user's original proposal, so the authorization scope for non-target cursors is inferred from the brief alone.

fable.result:
Review complete. Everything below comes from reading the frozen candidate-v2 packages against baseline, candidate-v1, both prior reviews, the governing references, the pinned donors, the provenance files, the fixtures, and the trial directories. I ran no executor, fetched nothing, and edited nothing.

**Verdict.** Candidate-v2 resolves every material finding from both prior rounds, and I found no new material unresolved objection. What remains is one provenance count error, one report-completeness item, two stale README lines held for finalization, and five low-severity wording or ordering preferences. Integrity checks all passed.

## Integrity and prior findings

- **Frozen state matches.** The working tree equals candidate-v2 for all five packages, and `candidate-v2-hashes.json` matches recomputed SHA-256 for all 29 files. The pstack LICENSE blob is identical at 23e4138, 7022c81, 9511e60 and e43c7ee, so existing notices stay valid. The architect delta is one commit touching two files. The error-handling delta is only the plugin version bump.
- **Trials are wired correctly.** Fixtures match the recorded baseline input hashes. Baseline arms carry baseline packages, candidate-behavior and candidate-fallback arms carry byte-identical candidate-v2 copies, and the fallback catalogs omit verify for debug and prototype. The candidate-architecture arm ran against candidate-v1's entrypoint, not v2, so the v2 wording at design-code-structure/SKILL.md:104-110 still has no execution evidence, as the brief already plans.
- **A1, A3/F3, A5 resolved.** Performance-related failures now reach the investigation reference at debug/SKILL.md:42-43 and investigation.md:3. The qualifier at verify/SKILL.md:30 keeps functional regressions benchmark-free. Dependency roles at debug/origin.txt:112-116 and prototype/origin.txt:62-66 plus both maintenance references at line 4-5 no longer claim "no skill dependency".
- **A2, A4, F7 resolved.** Adoption decisions require resolved or justified configuration differences at performance-evidence.md:35-39. Rejection and acceptance outcomes are separate at workflow-to-skill/SKILL.md:102-105, with unresolved proof kept at 109-110. Comparison definitions apply before running or are checked for supplied results at performance-evidence.md:16-17.
- **F1, F4, F5 resolved.** Compact fallbacks exist at investigation.md:83-85 and experiment.md:21-24, and prototype now passes the harness and rerun command at experiment.md:17. Supplied packets need no recipe at performance-evidence.md:7-9. Return without a new investigation is explicit at performance-evidence.md:75-77, and debug keeps measurement at investigation.md:80-81 and 92.
- **F2, F8, F9, F10 resolved.** Routing and executor naming sit at workflow-to-skill/SKILL.md:55-64 and 105-111, with extraction-only authority kept. Exposed representations return at design-code-structure/SKILL.md:104-105, and enforcement is named but implemented only within authorized implementation at 107-109.
- **F6 confirmed.** The reference contains no fixed run count, mandatory limiter, Linux commands, PR rule or hillclimb loop. Recording those deviations belongs to the held provenance step.

## Remaining findings

Necessary corrections, all outside the candidate instruction text:

- **The non-target range count is 17, not 15.** Fifteen non-target skills hold the ranges, but `pr` and `pr-followup` each carry two Matt or pstack sources. The provenance step must write 17 review records across 15 non-target origin files plus the 9 target ranges to reach 26.

| Group | Skills | Ranges |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Target | 5 | 9 |
| Non-target advancing | 15 | 17 |
| Already at candidate | 6 | 6 |

- **Seven other-author cursor/plugins sources stay at 23e4138.** They are commit and pr `cursor-reviewable-pr`, pr-followup `cursor-ci-followup` and `dyl-pr-readiness`, review-code-changes `thermos-review` and `cursor-quality-review`, and simplify-code `cursor-deslop`. Their scoped diffs to e43c7ee are empty. Excluding them is consistent with the author rule, since the three `cursor`-named ids inside the 32 record Lauren Tan as author. The final report should list them as unchanged Check findings so nobody reads the repository as fully synchronized against cursor/plugins.
- **Two README lines go stale.** README.md:137 says prototype's ordinary use has no skill dependency, which the new conditional verify dependency contradicts. README.md:352 should name the performance-evidence guidance beside the browser guidance. Both belong in the held README edit.
- **Staging caution.** The working tree still holds the pre-existing deletion of `walkthrough/SKILL.md` recorded in HANDOFF.md and snapshot.json. Stage the intended paths explicitly.

Low-severity preferences, none blocking:

- **Ordering.** investigation.md:77-79 asks for the verify call with retained results before line 87 says to measure. experiment.md:15-18 does the same before line 26 says to run the harness. Move the measurement sentence first or add "once measurements exist".
- **Scope of the prototype fallback.** experiment.md:21-24 reads as applying to every experiment, while baseline scoped repetitions, units and range to timing claims. Start the sentence with "For those claims" so behavior-only experiments are not asked for units and a range.
- **"Resolve" at performance-evidence.md:36.** It can read as equalize and rerun, which lines 39-40 forbid. "Account for, by evidence," states the intent.
- **Duplicate owner naming.** workflow-to-skill/SKILL.md:55 and 61 both name the existing enforcement owner. One is enough.
- **Absent mechanism.** design-code-structure/SKILL.md:107 could add "or state that none is available" for projects with no enforcement route.

Provenance record contents to include when the held step runs:

- **pstack-architect** should record the partial-context criterion, parallel routes, reachable internals and registry derivation as adapted, map split ownership to the existing invariant rule at state-and-boundaries.md:24-28, and skip the delete-in-the-same-change and build-must-fail absolutes.
- **pstack-correct** should record the valid-nearby-case proof as a local addition beyond the donor, and skip the twice threshold, rule table, exception expiry and approval, docs-last ordering, and repository edits.
- **pstack-performance-evidence** should skip the five-run minimum, mandatory limiter, uptime and nproc, tune-then-remeasure, single PR number, rank-sum test and hillclimb loop. It should list the three playbooks and prove-it-works as context read. Adding an e43c7ee revision line to the two pstack notices is optional since the blob is unchanged.

Behavioral notes for the grader: on my read both the baseline and candidate-v1 architecture outputs meet every grader must, including a named lint check left unimplemented at decision.md:3 and 162 and v1 preserved at 127-137, so expect "no regression" rather than an improvement claim. For the candidate debug and prototype arms, check that verify is named as supplied context without an invocation claim and that the run returns to diagnosis or the recommendation. For the fallback arms, check that counts, units and variation appear without any verify claim.

Limits: read-only consultation with no executor runs, host selection probes, or edits. I did not read candidate arm outputs beyond catalogs and hashes. The user's original Spanish proposal was not available to me, so scope statements rest on the brief. The 32-scope list was re-derived from the repository's origin files, which is how the 41 total and the 17-range count were established.
